_comment: Flagged language: slurs by group, stored ROT13-scrambled so they don't show up in the slang library, search results or code review. Both engines unscramble them in memory, and catch spellings like '@' for 'a', '*' in place of a vowel, repeated letters and spaced-out letters. 'when_joking' says what happens when the message has a laugh, 'jk' or a laughing emoji: 'ignore' (friends saying it to each other) or 'note' (a softer, yellow flag instead of red). 'phrases' are plain patterns (not slurs) that count the same way. Left out on purpose: the n-word ending in '-a' (widely used casually within Black communities and in Gen Z texting) and 'dyke' (reclaimed, and a sea wall), 'queer' (reclaimed), 'cracker', 'nip', 'slant' and 'kaffir' (everyday words or foods). To add a word: python3 -c "import codecs; print(codecs.encode('word', 'rot13'))", add it to a group, then run python3 tools/build_web.py.

aimed.label: {title} slur aimed at you
aimed.implication: A slur used against you. That's hate, and every app lets you report it.

used.label: Flagged language: {label}
used.implication: They used {label} language, even if not at you. Worth noticing how they talk about other people.

joking.label: Flagged language: {label} (as a joke)
joking.implication: A {label} slur said as a joke. Not aimed at hurting you, but it shows what they find funny.
